body:
Gold is trading in the mid-$4,300s to low-$4,400s today, which lines up with where both platforms are pricing their contracts. IFCM's live feed put spot at $4409.880 as of August 18, while FXStreet's commentary has gold recently touching a fresh two-month peak near $4,450 as rate-hike expectations for the Fed have eased. That backdrop explains why Kalshi's August settlement strikes cluster tightly around 50/50 in the $4,330–$4,370 range and why Polymarket's weekly touch $4,450 contract is already trading near 0.71–0.76 — the market thinks that level has been reached or is very close. Nothing here looks like a dislocation; it's ordinary pricing around a genuinely volatile month for gold.

The scanner flagged exactly one cross-platform opportunity today, and it's a good example of why these need a skeptical read rather than a straight buy signal. It pairs a Polymarket YES on gold touching $4,700 in August (ask 0.08) with a Kalshi NO on settling above $4,731.99 at August 31 (ask 0.91), for a claimed net edge of under half a cent per contract after fees and only $0.43 of total capturable profit. The catch is that these aren't the same bet: Polymarket's contract resolves on any intraday touch of $4,700, while Kalshi's resolves on the settle price at a specific time on August 31 against a different threshold ($4,731.99). A scenario exists — gold spikes above $4,700 intraday but settles back below $4,731.99 — where both legs pay out, but the reverse can also happen, so the guaranteed dollar isn't truly riskless. Given the razor-thin edge and mismatched strikes/resolution rules, this reads as a modeling artifact of treating two different underlyings as equivalent, not free money.

Beyond that one flagged pair, order books across both venues look normal for the size on offer, with no unusually wide bid-ask spreads or dead markets standing out. Overall, a quiet day: prices are internally consistent with each other and with where spot gold has actually been trading.
headline: Gold prices near $4,400 track cleanly across platforms; flagged arbitrage is a mismatch, not free money
